```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
tab <- \(f) read_csv(here("output", "tables", paste0(f, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
pct <- \(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")
w98 <- tab("step2_within_div_variance"); w99 <- tab("t99_within_cell_variance"); r2b <- tab("t99_cells_vs_phylo_r2")
g <- \(w, m, col) w[[col]][w$metric == m]
r2 <- \(r, m) r2b$r2_comp[r2b$resp == r & r2b$model == m]
```

**The question.** A decade ago it was often argued that phylogenetic diversity
(PD) should predict ecosystem function better than species richness, "in a range
of communities, from single-trophic to complex networks" (Srivastava et al. 2012,
*Ecol. Lett.*). The multitrophic part of that claim has rarely, if ever, been tested with
experiments that manipulated more than two trophic levels, which are rare (e.g. of 94 diversity manipulations synthesized by Lefcheck et al. 2015,
only 3 involved carnivores, each manipulating a single trophic group).

**Why these data.** The T98 (Downing & Leibold 2002, *Nature*) and T99 (Downing
2005, *Ecology*) experiments manipulated richness and composition of macrophytes,
grazers and predators simultaneously, measured productivity, respiration and
decomposition repeatedly, and imposed an acid pulse. They are among the very few
designs able to test the claim directly.

**Main results** (Bayesian mixed models; details in the attached report).

1. **Whole-community phylogenetic metrics mostly restate trophic structure.**
   Every composition is built from plants and animals, and the plant–animal
   split dominates phylogenetic distances. Once the design is accounted for,
   little independent variation remains in the metrics of the stocked
   communities: `r pct(g(w98, "PD_init", "within_div_share"))`
   (PD) and `r pct(g(w98, "MPD_init", "within_div_share"))` (MPD) in T98, and
   `r pct(g(w99, "PD_init", "within_cell_share"))`–`r pct(g(w99, "VPD_init", "within_cell_share"))`
   in T99 (panel A; VPD keeps more in T98, and realized compositions vary more
   because of extinctions and invasions).
2. **No robust effect of PD, MPD or VPD on productivity or respiration** at fixed
   richness or trophic design, for stocked or realized composition, in either
   experiment.
3. **Across trophic configurations (T99), one metric is an imperfect summary of
   food-web structure:** design cells (FG composition × richness) account for
   `r pct(r2("prod", "cells"))` / `r pct(r2("resp", "cells"))` of among-composition
   variance in productivity / respiration; the best single metric (VPD) for
   `r pct(r2("prod", "rich_VPD"))` / `r pct(r2("resp", "rich_VPD"))`; PD for
   ~0 (panel B).
4. **Disturbance:** the acid pulse depressed respiration by ≈ 1 SD, followed by
   recovery (stronger at the highest richness), consistent with Downing & Leibold
   (2010). Phylogenetic metrics did not robustly modulate resistance or recovery;
   a positive PD/MPD × recovery effect on decomposition in T99 was not replicated
   in T98 (exploratory).

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
shares <- bind_rows(
  w98 |> transmute(exp = "T98", metric, share = within_div_share),
  w99 |> filter(!str_detect(metric, "MNTD")) |> transmute(exp = "T99", metric, share = within_cell_share)
) |>
  separate(metric, c("metric", "composition"), sep = "_") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, c("PD", "MPD", "VPD")),
         composition = factor(composition, c("init", "final"), c("stocked", "realized")))
pA <- ggplot(shares, aes(metric, share, fill = composition)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~exp) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(stocked = "#7B1FA2", realized = "#F9A825")) +
  labs(title = "A. Variance of metrics left after the design", x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
pB <- r2b |> filter(model != "rich_only", resp != "dc") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, c("rich_PD", "rich_MPD", "rich_VPD", "cells"), c("PD", "MPD", "VPD", "design cells")),
         resp = recode(resp, prod = "productivity", resp = "respiration")) |>
  ggplot(aes(r2_comp, model)) + geom_point(size = 2) + facet_wrap(~resp) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "B. T99: among-composition variance explained", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1.1, 1))
```

**Proposed message.** In multitrophic communities, whole-community phylogenetic
diversity largely re-describes who eats whom; once trophic structure and
richness are controlled, it adds little. A phylogenetic "BEF shortcut" for food
webs therefore requires designs in which relatedness varies within trophic
levels, independently of trophic structure.

**Proposed target:** *Oikos* (Research article); fallback *Freshwater Biology*.
**Working title:** "Phylogenetic diversity restates trophic structure and does not
predict ecosystem functioning in experimental multitrophic food webs".

**Questions for you:** (i) Does this framing work for you? (ii) Amy: please confirm
the timing of the acid pulse in T99 (inferred between days 19 and 22) and that the
stocked compositions match your design. (iii) Any data or analyses you would add
or remove?
